- upper arm (shoulder–elbow), forearm (elbow–wrist)
- Derived: shoulder/hip, shoulder/torso, hip/torso, torso/leg, leg segments, arm segments
- Optional stretch: waist estimate via selfie-segmentation mask (narrowest torso cross-section); optional 3D segment lengths via pose_world_landmarks.

- One JSON object per image: every ratio rounded to 3 decimals, plus landmark visibility stats and warnings.
- Annotated copy per image with the skeleton drawn and landmark indices labeled, saved to an annotate/ dir. Numbers are not trusted until a human has eyeballed the annotated copies.

5. MODELING (the "body model")
- Aggregate across multiple photos of the same person into a per-person body model: mean ratio vector + per-ratio std, like a face-embedding centroid.
- Support comparison: distance between a new photo's ratio vector and stored body models (Euclidean on z-scored ratios), as an auxiliary signal alongside face matching.

6. CLI
- measure.py <image...> [--annotate-dir] → JSON to stdout
- model.py --person <name> <images...> → writes/updates models/<name>.json
- match.py <image> --models models/ → ranked matches with distances

- Before finalizing any ratio definition, verify landmark placement on annotated copies of 3+ varied test images (front, angled, mirror selfie).

8. ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- Runs end-to-end on a test photo with no warnings suppressed.
- JSON schema validates; annotated copy shows correct skeleton placement.
- A per-person model built from 3+ photos reports means and stds; std on shoulder/hip under 0.2 on clean frontal shots.
- match.py correctly ranks the right person first on held-out photos of two different people.
